key_insight: FracGen learns fracture-aware video generation from a single intact image by using physics-conditioned supervision to model how objects deform, crack, and tear in a controllable way.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a data-driven alternative to expensive per-scene fracture simulation, enabling more realistic damage prediction and control for graphics, robotics, and virtual testing workflows.
method: FracSim augments MPM simulation with a continuum damage model to generate paired fracture videos and dense physical fields.
FracGen jointly predicts RGB video and physics maps, so the network learns physical state rather than only surface appearance.
Physics-informed losses enforce consistency across predicted fields and improve crack progression realism and controllability.
evidence_signal: The paper introduces a fracture plausibility benchmark and reports that FracGen outperforms prior video generation baselines in both physical fidelity and visual quality.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on the realism and coverage of the simulation-derived training data, so extrapolation to unseen materials or loading conditions may be limited.
paper_title: FracGen: Learning How Objects Stretch and Tear with Physics-Informed Video Generation
